name: recruitment-receptor-baseline
title: Receptor realization: cue + receptor-gated response recruits
question:
Does a receptor-level realization of chemotactic recruitment -- where each
responder activates from naive to chemotaxing only once its per-cell
receptor-occupancy Hill relation crosses threshold -- reproduce the
baseline recruitment claim, using a cited receptor Kd instead of a
hand-tuned chemotaxis strength?
hypothesis:
With the cue secreted (rate 10) and the receptor-gated response intact
(chemo_lambda 14, kd 2.9 nM), responders whose Hill-occupancy crosses the
activation threshold chemotax up the gradient, and the recruitment index
rises well above zero, consistent with the phenomenological baseline.
objective:
Simulate the receptor-recruitment world (the recruitment_receptor
composite): naive(2)/activated(3) responder sub-types, each carrying a
ReceptorSubcell that computes Hill occupancy from the local cue field, and
measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps across 5 seeds.
description:
The receptor-level realization of the chemotactic-recruitment claim. Where
recruitment-baseline gives every responder a hardcoded, always-on
chemotactic bias, this study makes the response emergent: each responder
carries a per-cell ReceptorSubcell that reads the local cue concentration
and computes fractional receptor occupancy via a Hill relation (kd, hill,
conc_scale, activate_occupancy). Only once occupancy crosses threshold does
a responder flip from naive (type 2, non-chemotaxing) to activated (type 3,
chemotaxing) -- see
pbg_cpm_studies.composites.chemotaxis_receptor.recruitment_receptor. The
receptor's Kd is not a free-fit parameter: it is the CXCL8 monomer-CXCR1
affinity reported in Nasser et al. 2009 (2.9 nM), so activation is
calibrated to a real receptor-ligand pair rather than an arbitrary lambda.
The Kd calibration is recorded as a parameter (model_settings below), not
as a literature_target on the recruitment-index test -- recruitment index
is a 0-1 fraction, and a Kd-valued target on that test would corrupt any
divergence_factor computed from it.
claim:
Cue + receptor-gated response recruits: across 5 seeds the final
recruitment index is 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882), above the 0.5 pass
threshold, with responder activation gated by a receptor Kd cited to
Nasser 2009 rather than a hand-tuned chemotaxis strength.
expected_behavior: Responders whose receptor occupancy crosses the Hill activation threshold switch from naive to activated and chemotax up the gradient.
Recruitment index rises above 0.5 by the end of the run.

evidence.from_test: Responders are recruited to the source (receptor realization)
evidence.observed: recruitment index 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882) across 5 seeds, receptor-gated activation via a cited CXCR1 Kd (2.9 nM, Nasser 2009)

findings.statement:
The receptor-level realization reproduces the baseline recruitment claim:
across 5 seeds the final recruitment index is 0.5667 (95% CI
0.3451-0.7882), above the 0.5 pass threshold, with responder activation
gated by a per-cell Hill-occupancy receptor model calibrated to a cited
CXCL8-CXCR1 Kd rather than an arbitrary chemotaxis strength.

conclusion:
The receptor-level realization -- naive/activated responder sub-types
gated by a per-cell Hill-occupancy receptor model with a cited CXCL8-CXCR1
Kd -- reproduces the phenomenological baseline's recruitment claim
(recruitment index 0.5667 here vs 0.767 for the phenomenological
realization). Fidelity note: the Kd (2.9 nM, Nasser 2009) is a real
receptor-affinity value; conc_scale (the CPM field-unit -> nM mapping) and
hill/activate_occupancy remain modeling choices, not independently fit
(see model_settings).
key_assumptions: Same world geometry as recruitment-baseline (source slab + six responders, Moore-8 lattice, order 2).
Receptor occupancy is computed per responder each step from the local field via a Hill relation; activation is a one-way naive -> activated switch.
conc_scale maps the CPM field's raw amplitude into the Hill relation's nM-scale sensitive window; this mapping, not the Kd itself, is the simulation-unit calibration choice.
Recruitment radius = 15 px, identical to recruitment-baseline.
